manual.description:
This streams your BMW or Mini vehicle data into Home Assistant.

**First, set up CarData in the BMW portal** (skip if you already have a Client ID):

1. Open the [BMW CarData portal]({portal_url}) and sign in. If CarData isn't available in your country, sign in via the [UK]({portal_uk}) or [German]({portal_de}) portal — the Client ID works everywhere.
2. Create a **CarData Client** and copy the **Client ID** it shows you.
3. Subscribe the client to **both** services: **CarData API** and **CarData Streaming**.

Don't tick anything under **Data Selection** yet — after you authorise, the next screens let you choose which data to stream and turn it on with a one-click bookmarklet.

Then paste the **Client ID** below.

authorize_failed.title: Authorisation didn't finish
authorize_failed.description:
We couldn't complete the device authorisation.

**Details**
```
{error}
```

**What to check**
- **declined / access_denied (403):** BMW's server often reports a decline even after you approved — a known BMW-side issue. Retry in a **private/incognito window**: open the BMW CarData portal yourself (don't follow a link with a code in the URL), sign in, choose *Authenticate device* and **type the code by hand**. Also make sure the Client ID is subscribed to **both CarData API and CarData Streaming** before authorising, and that you're the **primary** user for the vehicle.
- **expired / timeout:** the code wasn't approved in time.

Press **Submit** to get a fresh code and try again. If it keeps failing, delete the CarData client in the BMW portal, create a new one, and re-authorise with the new Client ID — or email BMW support (bmwcardata-b2c-support@bmwgroup.com) quoting the **BMW reference** above.

A full walkthrough is in the integration's README under *Troubleshooting → Onboarding fails with "access denied"*.

progress.wait_for_authorization:
**Approve Home Assistant on the BMW/MINI sign-in page**

1. Open the **[authorisation page]({verification_url})** and sign in with your BMW/MINI account.
2. Type in this code when asked: **{user_code}**
3. Confirm the device.

**Enter the code by hand** — don't use a link with the code already in the URL, and make sure no old code is pre-filled. BMW's server often wrongly records a *decline* for pre-filled codes. If it fails anyway, retry in a private/incognito window.

Leave this dialog open — it continues automatically the moment you approve. There's nothing to click here.

init.description: Pick an action. The token and authorisation actions keep your connection alive; the data actions call BMW's REST API on demand (each counts against the daily 50-request API limit).

action_reauth.title: Re-authorise with BMW
action_reauth.description: Run BMW's device authorisation again — for example after the refresh token expired (every 2 weeks) or if you generated a new Client ID. You'll approve Home Assistant on BMW's website afterwards.

action_fetch_basic.description:
Fetch static details (model, colour, options) for every known vehicle.

Press Submit to continue.

action_fetch_tyre.title: Fetch tyre diagnosis
action_fetch_tyre.description:
Fetch the latest tyre-pressure diagnosis for your vehicles.

Press Submit to continue.

action_trips.description:
Reconstructs your drives from the stream at no API cost — distance, the business/private/commute split, consumption and a monthly review.

Set **Work zone** so commutes (home ↔ work) are recognised automatically; you can always correct a trip afterwards. Everything that isn't a commute is filed as the **Default type** (Private out of the box). A commute also survives a stop on the way: if the car stands no longer than the **Commute stop tolerance**, the drive there and the drive on are both counted as commuting. **Resolve addresses** is off by default: with it on, a trip endpoint outside any Home Assistant zone is looked up via OpenStreetMap and stored as an address — the coordinates are sent for the lookup but never saved.

**Record route** is also off by default: with it on, each trip stores its GPS track — where the car went and when — so a map can show and replay the drive. This is the only setting that saves raw coordinates to disk, including your exact start and end points.

**Trip-capture diagnostics** is a troubleshooting aid: with it on, every GPS fix, timer and message is logged in detail and a capture file is written, to help improve trip detection. Turn it on only for a test drive, then off again.

error.missing_token: No valid access token is available. Try "Refresh tokens now" or re-authorise first.

abort.reauth_started: Authorisation restarted. Finish the new login from the notification that just appeared.
abort.reauth_device_code_failed: BMW rejected the device authorisation request ({error}). Check the Client ID and try again.
abort.reauth_missing_client_id: Client ID is missing for this integration entry. Remove and re-add the integration to authorise again.
abort.reauth_failed: Re-authorisation could not be started. Try again from the integration options.

api_quota_exhausted.description: The {limit} requests-per-24h BMW CarData REST limit has been reached, so on-demand data (basic info, charging history, tyre diagnosis, vehicle image) can't be refreshed right now. The streaming data keeps flowing. The quota frees up again at {next_reset}.

stream_unauthorized.title: BMW CarData stream not authorised
stream_unauthorized.description: BMW has rejected the streaming connection as unauthorised (MQTT rc=5) for over {minutes} minutes and it hasn't recovered on its own. This usually means the tokens need renewing, or another CarData client is holding the single per-account stream. Try Configure → Refresh tokens now, then Re-authorise with BMW if it keeps failing, and disconnect any other CarData client.

fetch_tyre_diagnosis.name: Fetch smart maintenance tyre diagnosis
fetch_tyre_diagnosis.description: Fetch the smart-maintenance tyre diagnosis for a VIN and log the response.
